title: PRESSER | Yolett McPhee-McCuin - LA Tech Postgame (11-15-26)
text: All right, coach, give your opening statements on the win against Louisiana Tech 69 to 53. >> Um, I don't take wins for granted. Um, so I was grateful for the win. I have a lot of respect for Louisiana Tech. The history, the tradition, and their team this year, I expect them to do really well. Uh, we had to prep as if this was us playing a SEC opponent. And so, uh, I thought we started off really intentional. Uh, we hit our goals in the first half. Um, and then human nature kicked in and we started to just become complacent with the game because uh, my team felt like we already had it won. That's something that we would have to work on. Uh, there were some bright spots. Nevertheless, I thought um uh Desiree uh needed a night like this. We're going to need her next game versus Ohio State. I thought she did some really good things for us. Um and and we believe that she's capable of doing those night in and night out. So, overall, like I said, I'm grateful for the win. Uh but we have a lot of work to do. >> You touched on Desiree just obviously the injury coming into the season. How have you seen her rehab and progress to now earning herself a starting a part time? >> Yeah, I mean Dez has worked really hard in the off season on her body which has allowed her to get uh to move better, to feel better, and perform like she performed to tonight uh today. So um like I said, she really needed a game like this. So I was I was happy for her. Um, and um, I expect her to just continue to grow, her and Rachel, as there are 265 Fivers. U, we're going to need them when we play in top 25 matchups. >> That second half, um, like Louisiana Tech kind of defensively changed some things up, kind of gave y'all some different looks that caused some turnovers offensively. So, what exactly from your perspective, um, did you see that they were doing that kind of gave your offense some trouble? >> I don't think they did anything different. I just think we reacted differently. I think I thought we got uh relaxed. We knew that they were going to blitz the ball screens and uh we just got a little bit um relaxed and that's just human nature. Um as a coach it drives me nuts because I know what's ahead. You know, my my players, they stay in the moment. You know, as far as they're concerned, they're watching the scoreboard and they feel like, you know, it's it's over with. But at the same time, like I said, I think Louisiana Tech is a feisty team. They're a good team. I didn't sleep well last night after I watched them on film, so I have a lot of respect for them. But I don't think they changed anything. I felt like uh there was a lot of emphasis for my staff and I to make sure we came out and really be focused. And um you know, I would I would have wanted us to show that we had more stamina to to stay focused for the uh third and fourth quarter. But that's something we have to work on. >> Desire, I asked both them about what they thought the biggest improvement or area of improvement needed to be. They both said communication. What testament can you speak to that? >> Yeah, I mean, I guess I'm not alone. Every time I turn on the TV or listen on social media, there's a coach that's winning, that's talking about this new age and and them not uh communicating like we would want them to. Honestly, that's the cheat code right now, I think, for all teams that are trying to be um successful in this era of athletics. Um and communication is one of our pillars. Uh it's something that they don't do a lot because of all of the uh resources they have like cell phones and whatnot. They just don't have to communicate by voice in a verbal way. Uh but it's something that we're working on every day in practice. >> What does a game like this specifically do uh in preparation for what's coming Wednesday Ohio State? >> Well, um you know, I thought that they pushed us downhill. Ohio State has a downhill guard that's going to push us. Uh actually, I think she's an all-American and uh yeah, it's going to be a hostile environment and and that'll be different for us. uh um and um with this team. Uh but a game like this, I thought they tested our toughness a bunch and so we had to do a bunch of tough things and I thought we we did that for the most part. I hadn't seen film yet. So I'm cautious on what I said that I think we did well versus what I didn't think we did well. It's really why I don't meet with my team after the game is because I need to see what's going on before I before I speak. But um I thought that uh we challenged them to come out focused and um I felt like that that starting group was incredibly focused. Um and I told you all I'm going to change the lineup up until I'm really comfortable or it will be depending on our opponent. That's the kind of team we have. Um there were some bright spots though. I saw a lot of bright spots from certain people. Desiree Maya did some things that we have been really asking her to do. I'm just talking about like what stood out to me. And then I uh I I believe that Jay Tilman has been consistently just tough and we're just going to need that. So um what did it teach me? That we have a lot of work to do. [laughter] >> Coach, going into what you mentioned as a hostile environment, >> what is your message to this team? They haven't played together. They haven't played on the road yet. What's your message to this new team about going into an environment like that? >> Yeah. Um I I think right now it would just be consistent. We have to It'll be my consistent message. You know, if if we're going to do something, we have to do it together and we have to do it the Old Miss way, you know. Um I'm not going to have to pump them up for this game. They're going to be pretty pumped up for this game. They're going to want to come out and play well, for sure. Uh so that's taken care of. Now it's building good on good habits um and trying to lessen the bad ones. And so every time we play, I learn something new about my team as I'm watching them. Like just how they communicate with each other, things that frustrate them, things that um that we need to work through, and I'm just grateful for it. So regardless of of when we go down there, I mean, I don't we should never play a game not to win. So, we're going to go to play this game to win, but I'm really looking forward to the lessons that we gain, whether it's through a win or a loss. >> All right. Thank >> Thank you.
